readings.title: The Capture of Rabbah
readings.text: [2 Samuel 12:26] And Yo’aḇ fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and captured <dn>את</dn> the royal city. [27] And Yo’aḇ sent messengers to Dawiḏ, and said, “I have fought against Rabbah, and I have captured <dn>את</dn> the city of water. [28] “And now, gather <dn>את</dn> the rest of the people, and encamp against the city and capture it, lest I capture the city and it be called by my name.” [29] And Dawiḏ gathered <dn>את</dn> all the people and went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and captured it. [30] And he took <dn>את</dn> the crown of their sovereign from his head, its weight being a talent of gold, with precious stones. And it was set on Dawiḏ’s head. And he brought out the spoil of the city, a very great amount. [31] And he brought out <dn>את</dn> the people who were in it, and put them to work with saws and iron picks and iron axes, and made them pass through the brick kiln. And so he did to all the cities of the children of Ammon. And Dawiḏ and all the people returned to Yerushalayim. [1 Chronicles 20:2] And Dawiḏ took <dn>את</dn> the crown of their sovereign from his head, and found it to weigh a talent of gold, and there were precious stones in it. And it was set on Dawiḏ’s head. And he brought out the spoil of the city, a very great amount. [3] And he brought out <dn>את</dn> the people who were in it, and put them to work with saws, and with iron picks, and with axes. And so Dawiḏ did to all the cities of the children of Ammon. And Dawiḏ and all the people returned to Yerushalayim.

readings.title: Amnon's Sin Against Tamar
readings.text: [2 Samuel 13:1] And it came to be after this that Aḇshalom son of Dawiḏ had a beautiful sister whose name was Tamar, and Amnon son of Dawiḏ loved her. [2] And Amnon was so distressed over his sister Tamar that he became sick, for she was a maiden, and it was hard in the eyes of Amnon to do whatever to her. [3] But Amnon had a friend whose name was Yonaḏaḇ son of Shim‛ah, Dawiḏ’s brother. And Yonaḏaḇ was a very wise man. [4] And he said to him, “Why are you, the king’s son, becoming thinner day by day? Will you not tell me?” And Amnon said to him, “I love <dn>את</dn> Tamar, my brother Aḇshalom’s sister.” [5] And Yonaḏaḇ said to him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. And when your father comes to see you, say to him, ‘Please let my sister Tamar come and give me food, and prepare <dn>את</dn> the food before my eyes, so that I see it and eat from her hand <dn>את</dn> it.’ ” [6] So Amnon lay down and pretended to be sick. And the king came to see him, and Amnon said to the king, “Please let Tamar my sister come and make a couple of cakes for me before my eyes, so that I eat from her hand.” [7] And Dawiḏ sent to Tamar, to the house, saying, “Please go to the house of your brother Amnon, and prepare food for him.” [8] And Tamar went to her brother Amnon’s house, and he was lying down. And she took dough and kneaded it, and made cakes before his eyes and baked <dn>את</dn> the cakes. [9] And she took <dn>את</dn> the pan and served them before him, but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, “Make everyone go out from me.” And everyone went out from him. [10] And Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring <dn>את</dn> the food into the bedroom, and let me eat from your hand.” And Tamar took <dn>את</dn> the cakes which she had made, and brought them to Amnon her brother in the bedroom. [11] And she brought them to him to eat, but he took hold of her and said to her, “Come, lie with me, my sister.” [12] And she answered him, “No, my brother, do not humble me, for it is not done so in Yisra’ĕl. Do not do this folly! [13] “And I, where would I take my shame? And you, you would be like one of the fools in Yisra’ĕl. And now, please speak to the king, for he would not withhold me from you.” [14] But he would not listen to her voice, and being stronger than she, he humbled her and lay with <dn>את</dn> her. [15] And Amnon hated her with a very great hatred, so that the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, “Rise up, go!” [16] And she said to him, “No, for this evil of sending me away is worse than the other that you did to me.” But he would not listen to her. [17] And he called <dn>את</dn> his young man who served him, and said, “Now put <dn>את</dn> this one out, away from me, and bolt the door behind her.” [18] Now she had a long garment on, for the sovereign’s maiden daughters wore such garments. And his servant put <dn>את</dn> her out and bolted the door behind her. [19] And Tamar put ashes on her head, and tore <dn>את</dn> her long garment that was on her, and put her hand on her head and went away crying bitterly. [20] And Aḇshalom her brother said to her, “Has Amnon your brother been with you? But now, keep silent, my sister. He is your brother. Do not take this matter to heart.” And Tamar remained desolate in the house of her brother Aḇshalom. [21] And Sovereign Dawiḏ heard <dn>את</dn> all these matters, and he was very wroth. [22] And Aḇshalom did not speak to Amnon either good or evil, for Aḇshalom hated Amnon, because he had humbled <dn>את</dn> his sister Tamar.

readings.title: Aḇshalom's Revenge and Flight
readings.text: [2 Samuel 13:23] And it came to be, after two entire years, that Aḇshalom had sheepshearers in Ba‛al Ḥatsor, which is near Ephrayim. And Aḇshalom invited all the king’s sons. [24] And Aḇshalom came to the king and said, “See, your servant has sheepshearers. Please, let the king and his servants go with your servant.” [25] And the king said to Aḇshalom, “No, my son, let us not all go now, lest we be a burden to you.” And he urged him, but he would not go, and he blessed him. [26] And Aḇshalom said, “If not, please let my brother Amnon go with us.” And the king said to him, “Why should he go with you?” [27] But Aḇshalom urged him, and he let <dn>את</dn> Amnon and <dn>את</dn> all the king’s sons go with him. [28] And Aḇshalom commanded <dn>את</dn> his servants, saying, “See now, when the heart of Amnon is glad with wine, and I say to you, ‘Smite <dn>את</dn> Amnon!’ then you shall kill him. Do not fear, have I not commanded you? Be strong and be brave.” [29] And the servants of Aḇshalom did to Amnon as Aḇshalom had commanded. And all the king’s sons rose up, and each one mounted his mule and fled. [30] And it came to be, while they were on the way, that the report came to Dawiḏ, saying, “Aḇshalom has smitten <dn>את</dn> all the king’s sons, and not one of them is left!” [31] And the king rose up and tore <dn>את</dn> his garments and lay on the ground, and all his servants stood by with their garments torn. [32] And Yonaḏaḇ the son of Shim‛ah, Dawiḏ’s brother, answered and said, “Let not my master say they have killed all the young men, the king’s sons, for Amnon alone is dead. For by the command of Aḇshalom this has been purposed from the day that he humbled <dn>את</dn> his sister Tamar. [33] “And now, let not my master the king take the matter to his heart, to think that all the king’s sons are dead. For Amnon alone is dead.” [34] And Aḇshalom fled. And the young man who was keeping watch lifted up his eyes and looked, and saw many people coming from the road behind him, by the side of the mountain. [35] And Yonaḏaḇ said to the king, “Look, the king’s sons have come! As your servant said, so it is.” [36] And it came to be, as he had finished speaking, that look, the king’s sons came, and they lifted up their voice and wept. And the king and all his servants wept very bitterly. [37] But Aḇshalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihuḏ, sovereign of Geshur. And Dawiḏ mourned for his son every day. [38] So Aḇshalom fled and went to Geshur, and was there three years. [39] And Sovereign Dawiḏ longed to go to Aḇshalom, for he had been comforted concerning Amnon, because he was dead.

readings.title: Yo'aḇ's Plan to Return Aḇshalom
readings.text: [2 Samuel 14:1] And Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah knew that the king’s heart was toward Aḇshalom. [2] And Yo’aḇ sent to Teqoa and brought from there a wise woman, and said to her, “Please pretend to be a mourner, and put on mourning garments, please, and do not anoint yourself with oil, but act like a woman who has been mourning a long time for the dead. [3] “And go to the king and speak to him this word.” And Yo’aḇ put the words in her mouth. [4] And the woman of Teqoa spoke to the king, and she fell on her face to the ground and did obeisance, and said, “Save, O king!” [5] And the king said to her, “What is the matter with you?” And she answered, “Truly I am a widow, my husband is dead. [6] “And your maidservant had two sons. And the two of them strove together in the field, and there was no one to separate them, but the one smote <dn>את</dn> the other and killed him. [7] “And see, the whole clan has risen up against your maidservant, and they said, ‘Hand over <dn>את</dn> him who smote his brother, so that we put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed, and destroy <dn>את</dn> the heir also.’ And they would extinguish <dn>את</dn> my coal that is left, and leave to my husband neither name nor remnant on the earth.” [8] And the king said to the woman, “Go to your house, and I shall give orders concerning you.” [9] And the woman of Teqoa said to the king, “My master, O king, let the crookedness be on me and on my father’s house, and the king and his throne be guiltless.” [10] And the king said, “Whoever speaks to you, bring him to me, and he shall not touch you anymore.” [11] And she said, “Please let the king remember <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and do not permit the avenger of blood to destroy anymore, lest they destroy my son.” And he said, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the ground.” [12] And the woman said, “Please, let your maidservant speak another word to my master the king.” And he said, “Speak.” [13] And the woman said, “Why then have you planned such a matter against the people of <dn>Elohim</dn>? For the king speaks this word as one who is guilty, in that the king does not bring his banished one back. [14] “For we shall certainly die and be like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again. Yet <dn>Elohim</dn> does not take away a life, but <dn>He</dn> devises ways, so that <dn>His</dn> banished ones are not cast out from <dn>Him</dn>. [15] “And now, that I have come to speak <dn>את</dn> this word to my master the king, it is because the people have made me afraid. And your maidservant said, ‘Let me now speak to the king, it might be that the king performs <dn>את</dn> the word of his female servant. [16] ‘For the king would hear, to deliver <dn>את</dn> his female servant from the hand of the man who would destroy me and my son together from the inheritance of <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ [17] “And your maidservant said, ‘Let the word of my master the king now be comforting, for as a messenger of <dn>Elohim</dn>, so is my master the king to discern the good and the evil. And let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> be with you.’ ” [18] And the king answered and said to the woman, “Please do not hide from me the word that I am asking you.” And the woman said, “Let my master the king please speak.” [19] And the king said, “Is the hand of Yo’aḇ with you in all this?” And the woman answered and said, “As your being lives, my master the king, no one is able to turn to the right or to the left from all that my master the king has spoken. For it was your servant Yo’aḇ who commanded me, and he put <dn>את</dn> all these words in the mouth of your maidservant. [20] “To change <dn>את</dn> the appearance of the matter your servant Yo’aḇ did this matter. But my master is wise, according to the wisdom of a messenger of <dn>Elohim</dn>, to know <dn>את</dn> all that is in the earth.” [21] And the king said to Yo’aḇ, “See now, I have done <dn>את</dn> this word. Go, bring back <dn>את</dn> the young man <dn>את</dn> Aḇshalom.” [22] And Yo’aḇ fell to the ground on his face and did obeisance, and blessed the king. And Yo’aḇ said, “Today your servant knows that I have found favour in your eyes, my master, O king, in that the king has performed <dn>את</dn> the word of his servant.” [23] So Yo’aḇ arose and went to Geshur, and brought <dn>את</dn> Aḇshalom to Yerushalayim. [24] And the king said, “Let him return to his own house, but let him not see my face.” So Aḇshalom returned to his own house, and did not see the king’s face.

readings.title: Aḇshalom Reconciled to Dawid
readings.text: [2 Samuel 14:25] And in all Yisra’ĕl there was no one to be praised so much for his good looks as Aḇshalom. From the sole of his foot to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him. [26] And when he cut <dn>את</dn> the hair of his head – and it was at the end of every year that he cut it because it was heavy on him, so he cut it – he weighed <dn>את</dn> the hair of his head at two hundred sheqels according to the king’s standard. [27] And to Aḇshalom were born three sons, and one daughter whose name was Tamar. She was a woman of beautiful appearance. [28] And Aḇshalom dwelt two full years in Yerushalayim, but he did not see the king’s face. [29] Aḇshalom therefore sent for Yo’aḇ, to send him to the king, but he would not come to him. And he sent again a second time, but he would not come. [30] So he said to his servants, “See, Yo’aḇ’s field is near mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire.” And Aḇshalom’s servants set the field on fire. [31] Then Yo’aḇ arose and came to Aḇshalom’s house, and said to him, “Why have your servants set my field on fire?” [32] And Aḇshalom answered Yo’aḇ, “Look, I sent to you, saying, ‘Come here, so that I send <dn>את</dn> you to the king, to say, “Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me to be there still.” ’ And now, let me see the king’s face. And if there is crookedness in me, then let him put me to death.” [33] And Yo’aḇ went to the king and informed him. And he called for Aḇshalom, and he came to the king and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king. And the king kissed Aḇshalom.
